lessons.title: Introduce Yourself
lessons.description: Learn to write simple sentences to introduce yourself. Focus on basic personal information.

sections.heading: Using 'I am' for Name and Age
sections.content: When you introduce yourself, use 'I am' followed by your name or age. For example: 'I am Lan.' or 'I am 10 years old.'

sections.heading: Saying Where You Are From
sections.content: Use 'I am from' to tell people your country or city. For example: 'I am from Vietnam.' or 'I am from Hanoi.'

sections.heading: Start with Your Name
sections.content: Always start your introduction with your name. Then, add 1-2 more simple facts about yourself like your age or where you live.

essays.prompt: Write a short paragraph introducing yourself. Include your name, age, where you are from, and one thing you like to do.

lessons.title: Describe Your Room
lessons.description: Learn to describe your room using simple sentences and prepositions of place.

sections.heading: Using 'There is' and 'There are'
sections.content: Use 'There is' for one item (singular) and 'There are' for two or more items (plural). For example: 'There is a bed.' 'There are two chairs.'

sections.heading: Prepositions of Place
sections.content: Use words like 'in' (inside), 'on' (on top of), 'next to' (beside), 'under' (below) to say where things are. For example: 'My book is on the desk.'

sections.heading: Start with General Description
sections.content: Begin by describing if your room is big or small, and its color. Then, list 2-3 main items you have in your room.

fillBlanks.stemText: There is a ___ in my room.
There ___ a lamp on the desk.
I have many ___ in my room.

essays.prompt: Write a short paragraph describing your room. Mention its size, color, and 2-3 main items in it, using prepositions of place.

lessons.title: Write About Your Family
lessons.description: Learn to write simple sentences about your family members and what they are like.

sections.heading: Using 'I have' for Family Members
sections.content: Use 'I have' to talk about the members of your family. For example: 'I have a mother, a father, and one sister.'

sections.heading: Describing Family Members
sections.content: Use simple adjectives to describe your family members. For example: 'My mother is kind.' 'My father is tall.' 'My brother is funny.'

sections.heading: Introduce Each Member Simply
sections.content: Start by saying who is in your family. Then, for 2-3 members, say their name and one simple characteristic or what they do.

fillBlanks.stemText: I have one ___ and one sister.

essays.prompt: Write a short paragraph about your family. Mention who is in your family and describe 2-3 family members with simple adjectives.

lessons.title: My Favorite Food
lessons.description: Learn to write about your favorite food, describing its taste and why you like it.

sections.heading: Stating Your Favorite Food
sections.content: Use the sentence 'My favorite food is...' to introduce the food you like the most. For example: 'My favorite food is pho.'

sections.heading: Describing Food with Adjectives
sections.content: Use simple adjectives to describe the food. Examples: 'It is delicious.' 'It is sweet.' 'It is spicy.' 'It is healthy.'

sections.heading: Say Why You Like It
sections.content: After naming your favorite food, describe its taste or how it makes you feel. You can also mention when or where you eat it.

fillBlanks.stemText: I like to ___ it for dinner.

essays.prompt: Write a short paragraph about your favorite food. Name the food, describe its taste, and explain why you like it.

lessons.title: Describe a Pet
lessons.description: Learn to write simple sentences describing a pet, its appearance, and what it does.

sections.heading: Introducing Your Pet
sections.content: Start by saying 'I have a pet...' or 'My pet is a...' followed by the type of animal. For example: 'I have a pet dog.' or 'My pet is a cat.'

sections.heading: Describing Appearance
sections.content: Use adjectives to describe how your pet looks. Examples: 'It is small.' 'It has brown fur.' 'It has big eyes.'

sections.heading: Mention an Action
sections.content: After describing your pet's appearance, add one simple action it does. For example: 'It likes to play.' 'It sleeps a lot.'

fillBlanks.stemText: Max likes to ___ with a ball.

essays.prompt: Write a short paragraph describing a pet you have or a pet you like. Mention its type, name, appearance, and one thing it likes to do.

lessons.title: My School Day
lessons.description: Learn to write about your typical school day using simple present tense and time expressions.

sections.heading: Using Simple Present Tense for Routines
sections.content: Use the simple present tense to talk about things you do regularly, like your school day. For example: 'I go to school.' 'We study English.'

sections.heading: Time Expressions
sections.content: Use 'at' for specific times (e.g., 'at 7 o'clock') and 'in the morning/afternoon' for parts of the day. For example: 'I start school at 7 AM.'

sections.heading: List Main Activities
sections.content: Start by saying when your school day begins. Then, list 2-3 main activities you do at school and mention what you like about it.

essays.prompt: Write a short paragraph about your school day. Mention when it starts, 2-3 activities you do, and one thing you like about school.

lessons.title: The Weather Today
lessons.description: Learn to write simple sentences to describe the weather and what you can do.

sections.heading: Using 'It is' for Weather
sections.content: To describe the weather, use 'It is' followed by a weather adjective. For example: 'It is sunny.' 'It is rainy.' 'It is cold.'

sections.heading: Basic Weather Vocabulary
sections.content: Learn words like 'sunny', 'cloudy', 'rainy', 'windy', 'hot', 'cold', 'warm'. For example: 'It is a hot day.'

sections.heading: Connect Weather to Activities
sections.content: After describing the weather, you can add a simple sentence about an activity you can do or cannot do because of the weather. For example: 'It is sunny. I can play outside.'

essays.prompt: Write a short paragraph describing the weather today. Mention if it's sunny, rainy, hot, or cold, and one activity you can do or wear.

lessons.title: My Daily Routine
lessons.description: Learn to write about your daily activities using simple present tense and sequence words.

sections.heading: Using Simple Present Tense
sections.content: Use the simple present tense to describe actions you do every day. For example: 'I wake up.' 'I eat breakfast.' 'I go to school.'

sections.heading: Sequence Words
sections.content: Use words like 'First,' 'Then,' 'After that,' 'Finally' to show the order of your activities. For example: 'First, I wake up. Then, I brush my teeth.'

sections.heading: List 3-4 Main Activities
sections.content: Choose 3-4 important activities you do every day. Write them in order, starting from the morning, and use simple time expressions like 'at 6 AM' or 'in the evening'.

fillBlanks.stemText: Every morning, I ___ up at 6 AM.
In the evening, I ___ my homework.

essays.prompt: Write a short paragraph about your daily routine. Mention 3-4 main activities you do every day, using sequence words and simple times.

lessons.title: Describe a Color
lessons.description: Learn to write about your favorite color and give examples of things that have that color.

sections.heading: Stating Your Favorite Color
sections.content: Use the sentence 'My favorite color is...' to introduce the color you like the most. For example: 'My favorite color is blue.'

sections.heading: Naming Objects with the Color
sections.content: Give examples of things that are that color. For example: 'The sky is blue.' 'The ocean is blue.' 'My shirt is blue.'

sections.heading: Explain Why You Like It
sections.content: After naming the color and giving examples, you can add a simple reason why you like it. For example: 'I like blue because it is calm.'

fillBlanks.stemText: I ___ green because it is fresh.

essays.prompt: Write a short paragraph about your favorite color. Name the color, give 2-3 examples of things that are that color, and say why you like it.

lessons.title: My Best Friend
lessons.description: Learn to write about your best friend, describing their appearance, personality, and what you do together.

sections.heading: Introducing Your Best Friend
sections.content: Start by saying 'My best friend is...' followed by their name. For example: 'My best friend is Mai.'

sections.heading: Describing Personality and Appearance
sections.content: Use simple adjectives to describe your friend. Examples: 'She is kind.' 'He is funny.' 'She has long hair.' 'He is tall.'

sections.heading: Mention Shared Activities
sections.content: After describing your friend, add one or two simple sentences about what you like to do together. For example: 'We play games together.' 'We study together.'

essays.prompt: Write a short paragraph about your best friend. Mention their name, age, 1-2 characteristics (e.g., kind, funny), and one activity you do together.

lessons.title: Write a Short List
lessons.description: Learn to create simple lists using bullet points or numbers for clarity.

sections.heading: Using Bullet Points or Numbers
sections.content: When writing a list, you can use bullet points (•) or numbers (1., 2., 3.) to make each item clear and easy to read.

sections.heading: Simple Nouns for List Items
sections.content: For A1 level, keep your list items as simple nouns or short noun phrases. For example: 'apples', 'milk', 'a pen'.

sections.heading: Choose a Clear Category
sections.content: Before you start listing, decide on a category for your list (e.g., 'Things I need for school', 'My favorite fruits'). This helps keep your list focused.

fillBlanks.stemText: I need to make a shopping ___.
I will buy ___ at the store.

essays.prompt: Imagine you are going to school. Write a list of 5 things you need to bring with you.

lessons.title: My Favorite Animal
lessons.description: Learn to write about your favorite animal, describing its appearance, actions, and why you like it.

sections.heading: Stating Your Favorite Animal
sections.content: Use the sentence 'My favorite animal is...' to introduce the animal you like the most. For example: 'My favorite animal is a cat.'

sections.heading: Describing Appearance and Actions
sections.content: Use adjectives for appearance (e.g., 'It is big.' 'It has long legs.') and simple verbs for actions (e.g., 'It runs fast.' 'It eats grass.').

sections.heading: Explain Your Choice
sections.content: After describing the animal, add a simple sentence about why you like it. For example: 'I like lions because they are strong.'

fillBlanks.stemText: I ___ elephants because they are gentle.

essays.prompt: Write a short paragraph about your favorite animal. Name the animal, describe its appearance, one action it does, and why you like it.

lessons.title: Describe Your House
lessons.description: Learn to write simple sentences about your house, including its type and rooms.

sections.heading: Stating Your Home Type
sections.content: Start by saying 'I live in a house' or 'I live in an apartment.' For example: 'I live in a small house.'

sections.heading: Using 'There are' for Rooms
sections.content: Use 'There are' to mention the number of rooms. For example: 'There are three rooms in my house.' Then, name the rooms.

sections.heading: Describe 2-3 Main Rooms
sections.content: After mentioning the number of rooms, describe 2-3 main rooms (e.g., living room, bedroom, kitchen) and one simple item in each.

fillBlanks.stemText: There are three ___ in my house.
I have a living room, a kitchen, and a ___.
The living room is my favorite ___.
There is a TV ___ the living room.

essays.prompt: Write a short paragraph describing your house or apartment. Mention if it's big or small, how many rooms it has, and name 2-3 main rooms.

lessons.title: A Short Thank-You Note
lessons.description: Learn to write a simple thank-you note to express gratitude.

sections.heading: Starting and Ending Your Note
sections.content: Start with 'Dear [Name],' to address the person. End with 'Thank you,' or 'Best regards,' followed by your name.

sections.heading: Stating What You Are Thankful For
sections.content: Clearly state the reason for your thanks. Use 'Thank you for the [item]' or 'Thank you for your help.' For example: 'Thank you for the lovely gift.'

sections.heading: Keep it Short and Sincere
sections.content: For A1, keep your thank-you note very short and focus on one specific thing you are grateful for. One to two sentences are enough.

essays.prompt: Write a short thank-you note to a friend for a small gift they gave you. Mention the gift and say you like it.

lessons.title: My Favorite Game
lessons.description: Learn to write about your favorite game, describing what it is and who you play with.

sections.heading: Stating Your Favorite Game
sections.content: Use the sentence 'My favorite game is...' to introduce the game you like the most. For example: 'My favorite game is football.'

sections.heading: Describing the Game Simply
sections.content: Use simple adjectives (e.g., 'It is fun.' 'It is exciting.') and verbs (e.g., 'I play it with friends.' 'We run a lot.').

sections.heading: Mention Who You Play With
sections.content: After naming the game, say if it's an indoor or outdoor game, and who you usually play it with. You can also add why you like it.

fillBlanks.stemText: I ___ to play chess every weekend.

essays.prompt: Write a short paragraph about your favorite game. Name the game, say if it's indoor or outdoor, who you play with, and why you like it.

lessons.title: A Simple Postcard
lessons.description: Learn to write a very simple postcard message to a friend or family member.

sections.heading: Postcard Greetings and Closings
sections.content: Start with 'Dear [Name],' or 'Hello from [Place]!'. End with 'Best regards,' 'See you soon,' or 'Love,' followed by your name.

sections.heading: Short, Simple Sentences
sections.content: Postcards have limited space. Use 1-2 very simple sentences to convey your message. Focus on where you are and what you are doing.

sections.heading: Mention Location and Weather
sections.content: A good postcard often mentions where you are and what the weather is like. You can also add one simple activity you did or will do.

essays.prompt: Imagine you are on a short holiday. Write a simple postcard message to a friend. Mention where you are, what the weather is like, and one activity you did.

lessons.title: My Morning Routine
lessons.description: Learn to write about your morning activities using simple present tense and time expressions.

sections.heading: Using Simple Present Tense
sections.content: Use the simple present tense to describe actions you do every morning. For example: 'I wake up.' 'I eat breakfast.' 'I go to school.'

sections.heading: Time Expressions for Morning
sections.content: Use 'at' for specific times (e.g., 'at 6:30 AM') and 'then,' 'after that' to show the order of events. For example: 'First, I wake up. Then, I brush my teeth.'

sections.heading: List 3-4 Key Activities
sections.content: Focus on 3-4 main things you do every morning, from waking up until you leave for school or work. Write them in order.

fillBlanks.stemText: I ___ my teeth and wash my face.
Then, I ___ breakfast with my family.
My morning routine is always the ___.

essays.prompt: Write a short paragraph about your morning routine. Mention 3-4 activities you do every morning, using sequence words and simple times.

lessons.title: Describe a Photo
lessons.description: Learn to write simple sentences to describe what you see in a photo.

sections.heading: Introducing the Photo
sections.content: Start by saying 'This is a photo of...' or 'In this photo, I see...' to introduce the subject. For example: 'This is a photo of my family.'

sections.heading: Describing People and Objects
sections.content: Use simple sentences to describe who or what is in the photo. Use 'is' or 'are'. For example: 'My mother is on the left.' 'There are two children.'

sections.heading: Mention Location and Action
sections.content: After identifying the people or objects, mention where they are (e.g., 'at the park') and one simple action they are doing (e.g., 'They are smiling.').

fillBlanks.stemText: This is a ___ of my family.
My sister is ___ a red dress.

essays.prompt: Describe a photo of your family. Mention who is in the photo, where they are, and one thing they are doing.

lessons.title: Write About Today
lessons.description: Learn to write simple sentences about what you did or will do today.

sections.heading: Starting with 'Today is...'
sections.content: Begin by stating the day of the week and maybe the weather. For example: 'Today is Monday. It is sunny.'

sections.heading: Using Simple Present for Plans/Habits
sections.content: For A1, focus on what you usually do or what you plan to do today. For example: 'I go to school.' 'I will read a book.'

sections.heading: Mention 2-3 Activities
sections.content: After the introduction, list 2-3 main activities you did or will do today. You can also add how you feel about the day.

fillBlanks.stemText: In the afternoon, I will ___ with friends.

essays.prompt: Write a short paragraph about your day today. Mention what day it is, the weather, and 2-3 activities you did or will do.

lessons.title: Simple Numbers and Prices
lessons.description: Learn to write simple numbers and express basic prices for items.

sections.heading: Writing Numbers as Words
sections.content: Practice writing numbers from one to ten as words. For example: 'one', 'two', 'three', 'four', 'five', 'six', 'seven', 'eight', 'nine', 'ten'.

sections.heading: Expressing Simple Prices
sections.content: Use 'It is [number] VND' or 'It costs [number] VND' to state prices. For example: 'It is 10,000 VND.' 'The book costs 50,000 VND.'

sections.heading: Practice with Common Items
sections.content: Think of common items you buy (e.g., a pen, a book, an apple) and practice writing their names and simple prices.

fillBlanks.stemText: There are ___ books on the table.

essays.prompt: Imagine you are at a small shop. Write a list of 3 items you want to buy and their simple prices (e.g., A pen: 5,000 VND).
